claims.text: Press Gazette's tracker counted at least 3,434 journalism job cuts in the UK and US in 2025, at least 3,875 in 2024 and about 6,000 in 2023.
claims.quote: counted at least 3,434 journalism job cuts in the UK and US in 2025, at least 3,875 in 2024, and about 6,000 in 2023

value.unit: journalism job cuts in the UK and US

claims.text: The tracker's 2026 page has the BBC expecting to cut between 1,800 and 2,000 jobs.
claims.quote: the BBC expecting to cut between 1,800 and 2,000 jobs

claims.text: The Washington Post is cutting a third of all staff, including more than 300 of about 800 journalists.
claims.quote: the Washington Post cutting a third of all staff including more than 300 of about 800 journalists

claims.text: Reach plans to cut about 220 editorial jobs and create 60; what the 60 are is the signal.
claims.quote: Reach planning to cut about 220 editorial jobs and create 60

claims.text: Scripps is cutting 268 jobs as it embraces AI for a revolution in programming, its chief executive leaning into AI, automation and centralisation.
claims.quote: Scripps cutting 268 jobs as it "embraces AI for a 'revolution' in programming"

claims.text: In McClatchy's cuts across at least 13 titles the Idaho Statesman lost 10 of 18 reporters and three of four editors, and less than a week later the company's AI lab announced five hires.
claims.quote: the Idaho Statesman lost 10 of 18 reporters and three of four editors

value.unit: reporters lost at the Idaho Statesman

claims.text: A hiring decision is a direction of travel, the clearest statement a publisher makes about where its centre of gravity is going, because it is what the company actually spent.
claims.quote: A hiring decision is a direction of travel.

claims.text: Every organisation has a centre of gravity, the place where the thing it exists to make is made and where the power is; in a news publisher that is the journalists.
claims.quote: the place where the thing it exists to make is made, and where, if you look honestly, the power is

claims.text: Fire journalists and hire for traffic, engagement and content operations, the common case, and the centre moves to packaging inputs everyone else has.
claims.quote: Hire for traffic, engagement and content operations, which is the common case, and the centre moves to packaging.

claims.text: If success is measured by engagement the organisation reorganises around opening pages; optimise for that and you get clickbait whether or not anyone wants it, because the metric wants it.
claims.quote: Optimise for that metric and you get clickbait, whether or not anyone in the building wants it.

claims.text: This site runs on a different metric: pay after you read charges for how far a reader read and asks how useful it was, and nothing is placed to make them scroll.
claims.quote: This site runs on a different metric, and the difference is the point.

claims.text: The metric is a hiring plan in disguise; that is the sentence the owner would put to a board.
claims.quote: The metric is a hiring plan in disguise.

claims.text: Facebook referrals to publishers are down 58% in six years.
claims.quote: Facebook referrals to publishers down 58% in six years

value.unit: per cent fall in referrals over six years

claims.text: American newspaper newsrooms fell from about 71,000 jobs to about 31,000 between 2008 and 2020, a loss of 57%.
claims.quote: American newspaper newsrooms down from about 71,000 jobs to about 31,000 between 2008 and 2020, a loss of 57%

claims.text: Answer engines fetched a small publisher's pages 16,000 times in a week and sent 10 readers back.
claims.quote: answer engines fetching a small publisher's pages 16,000 times in a week and sending 10 readers back

value.unit: fetches in a week, against 10 readers sent back

claims.text: The attention business is getting smaller and harder every year, and a publisher that moves its centre of gravity into it is moving into a shrinking room.
claims.quote: The attention business is getting smaller and harder every year

claims.text: A publisher with journalists and no engineers fails the other way: the journalism is done and nothing enables it, no graph, no provenance, no versions, no agent surfaces, no meter.
claims.quote: The journalism is done, and then nothing enables it.

claims.text: Jonathan Palmer wrote that this is not about replacing journalists with engineers, because journalistic expertise and networks create the underlying advantage.
claims.quote: This isn't about replacing journalists with engineers. Journalistic expertise and their networks create the underlying advantage.

claims.text: Keep the journalists and tool them, with the tooling handed over as this makes you better, never this is going to replace you.
claims.quote: Keep the journalists, and tool them.

claims.text: Hire the roles that turn a notebook into a graph, historians, cartographers, ontologists and librarians, as people with the same role files the site's agents have, AI-enabled.
claims.quote: Hire the roles that turn a notebook into a graph.

claims.text: Hire the engineers and the AI product managers who build the back end, the provenance, the versions, the surfaces and the meter, not instead of the journalists but for them.
claims.quote: Not instead of the journalists. For them.

claims.text: The parable the owner keeps coming back to: a fast-growing competitor says we hire the ones you let go, and in publishing right now the good ones being let go are the journalists.
claims.quote: we hire the ones you let go

claims.text: The centre of gravity is visible from outside in five counts: original share, sourcing, corrections, roles hired against roles cut, and the metric the publisher itself reports.
claims.quote: The centre of gravity is visible from outside, in five counts

claims.text: Corrections must propagate is the standard for the third count; few publishers meet it, and this newsroom does not yet either.
claims.quote: few publishers meet it, and we do not yet either

claims.text: Run on this site, the honest result would be original share high, sourcing high, corrections kept but not propagating, roles all agents and one person, and a reader-value metric with almost no readers yet.
claims.quote: roles all agents and one person, and a metric that measures value to the reader with almost no readers yet

claims.text: The newsroom's agents already do most of the five counts on other people's content, as they did for twenty-one World News Day op-eds.
claims.quote: as they did for twenty-one World News Day op-eds

claims.text: The tracker is a tracker: its figures are for the UK and US, described as at least, and the 2026 page has no running total.
claims.quote: The tracker is a tracker.

claims.text: The owner does not know the inside of any of these decisions; the argument is about what the decision signals and what the metric does, not any publisher's motives.
claims.quote: I do not know the inside of any of these decisions.

claims.text: The parable is unsourced: the owner has heard it attributed to more than one company and cannot verify any of them.
claims.quote: I have heard it attributed to more than one company and I cannot verify any of them.

claims.text: This site is not a publisher at scale: seventy-odd articles by one author, written from voice memos by agents, is a working example of the stack, not proof a newsroom of two hundred can adopt it.
claims.quote: This site is not a publisher at scale.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 12 October 2026, written by the site's agent, with the figures from Press Gazette's tracker read that day.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 12 October 2026, written by this site's agent in the voice of this site.
